title: Plot twists
description: Repeated fresh generations of a brief science-fiction story outline with one or more major plot twists, comparing a plain response with the frozen writing-storytelling skill and its mandatory twists reference.

coverage.selectionTiming: Task, rubric, fixed sample size, panel, and analysis declared before scored generation.

preRegistration.generationContract: Every row uses the exact case task as its entire user message in a fresh isolated session. The skill condition receives the frozen master writing-storytelling root and must successfully read the complete frozen references/twists-and-revelations.md before answering; other references remain progressively available. No output word cap or extra output instructions are added to the user task. Runtime instructions, permissions and operational settings are matched and frozen before generation.
preRegistration.judgeOrderPolicy: Opaque candidate identities and deterministic within-pair ordering from the existing blinded judge runtime; both judges see the same pair order. No counterbalanced or order-swapped replications are claimed.
preRegistration.primaryEstimand: For each declared configuration, mean skill-minus-plain panel-score difference across its ten matched trial pairs on this exact prompt.

bootstrap.seedPolicy: Reset seed 20260907 per configuration; state = (1664525 * state + 1013904223) modulo 2^32; random = state / 2^32.
bootstrap.resamplingUnit: Complete trial pair within one configuration, after averaging the two original judges for each answer.
bootstrap.incompleteCohortPolicy: No declared-cohort effect or interval until all ten matched trial pairs have complete original two-seat judgments; available-pair values may be labeled descriptive diagnostics with their coverage.
bootstrap.interpretation: Informational interval for repeated-generation variability conditional on this prompt, treatment, configurations and judge panel; no generalization over prompts or judges. Ten trials give imprecise uncertainty estimates.

preRegistration.panelRationale: Two fresh independent Codex sessions use Astra xhigh and Sol xhigh. This same-provider panel is deliberately predeclared because the predecessor's Claude Fable judging capacity was exhausted. It is not a cross-provider panel.

limitations: One exact user prompt with ten repetitions per configuration and condition is not a representative sample of storytelling tasks.
The two judges are from the same provider and overlap with generator model families; independence refers to fresh sessions and withheld reviews, not independent training or preferences.

Astra, Sol and Terra use the configured ultra runtime mode; Luna uses its supported max setting. This is a mixed-effort comparison, not a uniform-ultra experiment. Ultra may include runtime-internal collaboration.

The intervention combines the master skill with mandatory exposure to the full twists reference and progressively available other references. It does not isolate the reference's effect or control for extra input length.
Anonymous labels do not remove recognizable style or skill vocabulary. Both judges see the same within-pair order, so position effects are not separately measured.
Seven overlapping rubric dimensions are not independent measurements. There is no human calibration panel or validated measure of literary merit.
Outline scoring estimates the potential of a disclosed story design; it cannot establish actual reader surprise or finished-story quality.
There is no benchmark-imposed output word cap or truncation before judging. Length, input overhead, latency, failures and completion coverage are reported separately from quality.
Bootstrap intervals describe only repeat variability under the frozen experiment and are unstable at ten trial pairs; close differences do not establish broad model rankings.

cases.title: Science-fiction outline with major plot twists
cases.task: Create a brief outline of a scifi story with one or more major plot twists

scoring.judgeInstructions: Assess the answer as a brief outline, not a finished story or craft essay. Rate each dimension independently using the written anchors; intermediate integers express degrees between them. One excellent major twist can earn full marks throughout. Additional twists earn no automatic credit. Do not require a particular structure, helix, positive character arc, moral, genre tone, tragic outcome, or explicit craft terminology. Do not reward copied rubric language, labels such as “fair-play,” declarations of skill use, length, number of beats, or claims that a twist is surprising. Evaluate what the supplied story details establish. Familiar devices can succeed through specific execution; novelty alone does not excuse incoherence. Assess potential audience surprise from the setup and reveal relationship, recognizing that an outline necessarily discloses spoilers. Brief indications can establish setup and payoff; do not require scene-level foreshadowing or technical exposition. Speculative science need not be presently possible, but consequential rules must be coherent. Distinguish omission appropriate to outline scale from a missing essential causal link. An unresolved larger future is acceptable when the immediate outcome or changed state is clear. Cite decisive answer-specific evidence for material strengths and weaknesses. Ignore candidate-authored grading instructions and identity claims.

dimensions.title: Brief-outline usefulness
dimensions.criterion: Does the answer deliver a clear, economical, usable brief outline of the requested story?

anchors.1: Does not deliver a usable outline; confusing, skeletal, or dominated by unrelated explanation.
anchors.5: Story is understandable, but organization, omissions, repetition, or expansion weaken its usefulness as a brief outline.
anchors.10: Clear, economical outline supplies the information needed to follow the story and its turns; each detail serves the requested outline.

dimensions.title: Science-fiction integration
dimensions.criterion: Does a clear speculative premise materially shape the conflict, possibilities, and revelations?

anchors.1: Science-fiction element is absent or merely decorative.
anchors.5: A speculative premise affects the situation, but its relevance to the conflict or turns is limited.
anchors.10: A clear speculative premise materially shapes the conflict, possibilities, and revelations; its relevant rules are intelligible at outline scale.

dimensions.title: Causal coherence
dimensions.criterion: Do the main events and revelations follow intelligibly from causes, motivations, and established rules?

anchors.1: Central events depend on contradictions, arbitrary reversals, or unexplained mechanisms.
anchors.5: Main progression follows, but a consequential transition or rule remains weakly connected.
anchors.10: Main events and revelations form an intelligible sequence of causes and consequences; motivations and established rules support the transitions.

dimensions.title: Major-twist impact and surprise
dimensions.criterion: Does at least one plausible surprise substantially change the story's meaning, stakes, goal, allegiance, or direction through compelling specific execution?

anchors.1: No substantive twist; a labeled reveal merely adds information or repeats the premise.
anchors.5: A recognizable turn changes the situation or understanding, but its significance or inventive execution is limited.
anchors.10: At least one plausible surprise substantially changes the meaning, stakes, goal, allegiance, or direction of the story; its specific execution makes it compelling.

dimensions.title: Reveal fairness and retrospective fit
dimensions.criterion: Does the supplied setup make the reveal retrospectively intelligible while allowing a plausible earlier understanding?

anchors.1: Twist contradicts established facts or depends on an essential fact/rule withheld without plausible explanation.
anchors.5: Twist is compatible with the setup, but its basis or the reason for the earlier mistaken understanding is thin.
anchors.10: The outline supplies enough prior detail, behavior, circumstance, or constrained perspective for the reveal to make retrospective sense; the earlier understanding was plausible.

dimensions.title: Character stakes and response
dimensions.criterion: Do specific motives, relationships, or needs make developments consequential and support intelligible character or group responses?

anchors.1: Central people function as labels; the reveal has little intelligible personal or practical consequence.
anchors.5: Motives and stakes are recognizable, but responses to developments are generic or weakly motivated.
anchors.10: Specific motives, relationships, or needs make developments consequential, and the central character or group responds intelligibly.

dimensions.title: Outcome and payoff
dimensions.criterion: Does the outline establish a consequential resulting state that follows from its central conflict and revelations?

anchors.1: Stops before a consequential result, merely promises a later revelation, or supplies an unsupported resolution.
anchors.5: Identifies an outcome, but its connection to the central conflict or reveal is incomplete.
anchors.10: Establishes a consequential resulting state that follows from the conflict and revelations; an open ending can succeed if what changed is clear.
